claim: FunSearch, an evolutionary procedure pairing a frozen LLM with a systematic external evaluator and best-shot prompting (feeding highest-scoring prior programs back into the next prompt), discovered new cap set constructions improving the asymptotic lower bound on cap set capacity from 2.2180 to 2.2202 -- the largest improvement in 20 years to an open extremal-combinatorics problem.
stance_target: the target paper's thesis that iterative LLM feedback degrades rather than improves search/design outcomes
scope_conditions: cap set problem in extremal combinatorics, Codey LLM (PaLM2-based), ~10^6 total samples
quoted_support: This discovery alone already improves the lower bound on the cap set capacity from 2.2180... [to] a new lower bound on the cap set capacity of 2.2202
numbers: cap set of size 512 in n=8

claim: FunSearch's iterative loop is not LLM self-critique; it combines a frozen LLM (deliberately chosen for fast inference over higher quality) with a hard external evaluator that discards incorrect programs and scores correct ones, plus an island-based genetic algorithm explicitly engineered to preserve population diversity and avoid collapse to local optima.
stance_target: mechanistic distinction between self-critique-driven iteration (which the mechanism literature shows degrades output) and external-verifier-driven evolutionary iteration (which this paper shows improves output)
quoted_support: FunSearch (short for searching in the function space) combines a pretrained (frozen) LLM, whose goal is to provide creative solutions, with an evaluator, which guards against confabulations and incorrect ideas... we maintain a large pool of diverse programs by using an island-based evolutionary method that encourages exploration and avoids local optima.
numbers: k=2 programs per prompt (diminishing returns beyond)

claim: The authors report FunSearch's results are not highly sensitive to the specific choice of LLM, as long as the model was trained on a sufficiently large code corpus, suggesting the success of feedback-driven iteration in this setting is not narrowly dependent on frontier-scale model capability.
stance_target: the hypothesis that feedback-driven iterative improvement is strictly model-scale/capability dependent and should not be expected from smaller models
scope_conditions: cap set and bin packing domains, code-pretrained LLMs of varying scale/quality
quoted_support: we have empirically observed that the results obtained in this paper are not too sensitive to the exact choice of LLM, as long as it has been trained on a large enough corpus of code.

claim: FunSearch discovered new heuristics for online bin packing that improve on widely used baseline heuristics on well-studied problem distributions, demonstrating generality of the iterative LLM+evaluator approach beyond the cap set problem.
stance_target: the target paper's thesis that iterative LLM feedback degrades rather than improves proposals, tested here in a second, distinct combinatorial optimization domain
quoted_support: We showcase the generality of FunSearch by applying it to an algorithmic problem, online bin packing, finding new heuristics that improve on widely used baselines.
